h1: The 7 Best Swivel TV Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Swivel TV Stands 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 swivel TV stands, from tabletop bases to floor stands and consoles, scored on swivel range, weight rating and TV size.
summary: The FITUEYES Floor TV Stand with Swivel is the best swivel stand for big screens: it supports TVs from 50 to 85 inches and carries 143 lb. The WALI Floor Stand brings a 60 degree swivel and built-in outlets, and the Perlegear is the widest-turning tabletop base. If you already own a dresser, the HOLMAXD and PERLESMITH bases are the inexpensive route.
intro: People buy a swivel stand because the TV has to serve two spots, say a sofa and the kitchen island, and then discover the swivel is the least reliable part of cheap stands. The advertised angle often counts both directions combined, so a stand that turns 30 degrees can mean 15 degrees each way. Read whether the number is total or per side before you trust it.

We ranked seven swivel stands across three styles: floor stands that carry the TV on a column, tabletop bases that sit on furniture you own, and one media console with a built-in swivel mount. Swivel range, weight rating, TV size support and stability led the scoring. Outlets, height levels and warranty length separated close finishes.

products.name: FITUEYES Floor TV Stand with Swivel
products.verdict: A 40 degree floor stand for 50 to 85 inch TVs rated at 143 lb.
products.description:
FITUEYES makes a standalone floor stand with a 40 degree swivel, a 10mm tempered glass shelf and a VESA pattern up to 800x600mm. It fits 50 to 85 inch TVs and is rated for 143 lb, the highest load of any swivel stand here.

That capacity is what puts it first. Most swivel bases in this list stop at 88 to 110 lb, which is tight for a modern 75 inch set plus a soundbar. The 10mm glass shelf is also thicker than the 8mm glass on the Rfiver. It needs no furniture beneath, so it solves living rooms where there is nothing to set a base on. The WALI offers a wider turn but at a lower weight limit.

Buy it if you have a large TV and no dresser. The caveat is the footprint of a floor stand, which needs clear space behind it.
products.idealFor: Owners of a large TV with no furniture suitable for a tabletop base.

products.name: WALI Floor TV Stand with Power Outlet
products.verdict: A 60 degree swivel floor stand with 3 AC and 2 USB outlets built in.
products.description:
WALI's floor stand turns 60 degrees and fits 32 to 75 inch TVs, with 3 height levels and a 110 lb capacity. Its standout is the 3 AC plus 2 USB outlets built into the column, backed by a 10-year warranty.

Built-in power is a real convenience, because a floor stand puts the TV far from the wall and the cords run exposed. WALI gives you the outlets so only one cord crosses the room. It ranks second to the FITUEYES because the load is lower, 110 lb against 143, and the size range stops at 75 inches. Against the Rolanstar console, it is simpler and swivels more widely.

Buy it if your room has few outlets or you want a tidy cord run. The caveat is that only 3 height levels limit fine eye-line tuning.
products.idealFor: Rooms with few outlets where the TV floats away from the wall.
products.skipIf: You own a heavy 80 inch TV.

products.name: Perlegear Universal Swivel Stand Base (PGTVS26)
products.verdict: A tabletop base with 60 degrees of total swivel and 8 degrees of tilt.
products.description:
The Perlegear PGTVS26 is a tempered glass tabletop base fitting 32 to 70 inch TVs, with 60 degrees of total swivel, 8 degrees of tilt and 9 height levels. It carries 88 lb.

The 8 degree tilt is the unusual part, since most tabletop bases only turn. Tilt lets you angle the screen down toward a sofa when the base sits high on a console. That feature, plus the 9 height levels, earns it third place. The 88 lb limit is where it gives ground: a 70 inch TV can come close to that rating, so weigh the set. Compared with the PERLESMITH, it turns twice as far and adds tilt for the same kind of price.

Buy it if you have a console and want maximum aiming flexibility. The caveat is that 60 degrees is a total, so expect 30 each way.
products.idealFor: Console owners who want to aim a mid-size TV precisely.
products.skipIf: Your TV is near 70 inches and heavy.

products.name: Rolanstar TV Stand with Swivel Mount and LED
products.verdict: A 59.1 inch media console with an integrated 34 degree swivel mount.
products.description:
Rolanstar's console is 59.1 inches wide and includes a swivel mount with 34 degrees of turn for 32 to 70 inch TVs. It adds 4 AC outlets plus USB, a 7-color 21-mode LED, and a height adjustable from 53 to 56 inches.

This is the only stand in the ranking that replaces both your furniture and your TV mount. The console storage is an advantage over the floor stands, and the 53 to 56 inch height raises the screen above a typical console. It ranks fourth because it lists no weight capacity and costs the most. The swivel is 34 degrees, narrower than the WALI.

Buy it if you are furnishing a room from scratch. The caveat is the missing load rating, which you should confirm before mounting a large screen.
products.idealFor: People furnishing a room who want storage and swivel together.
products.skipIf: You need a stated weight rating or want to spend less.

products.name: PERLESMITH Universal Swivel Tabletop Stand (PSTVS13)
products.verdict: A 30 degree tabletop swivel for 37 to 75 inch TVs with a 10-year warranty.
products.description:
The PSTVS13 swivels 30 degrees on a tempered glass base, supports 37 to 75 inch TVs, has 9 height levels and carries 99 lb. PERLESMITH backs it for 10 years.

The 99 lb rating beats the Perlegear and HOLMAXD, which stop at 88 lb, and that helps with big TVs. The swivel is the narrowest of the tabletop group, 30 degrees against 60, which is why it sits fifth. Against the FITUEYES floor stand, it needs a dresser but costs far less.

Buy it if you have furniture rated for the load and want the longest warranty. The caveat is the swivel range, which only suits turning slightly toward a sofa, not toward a second room.
products.idealFor: Dresser owners who want a long warranty and a modest swivel.
products.skipIf: You need a wide turn to face two areas.

products.name: HOLMAXD Universal Swivel Stand
products.verdict: A 60 degree tabletop base for 27 to 60 inch TVs with a dual safety lock.
products.description:
HOLMAXD sells a tempered glass tabletop base with 60 degrees of total swivel, 9 height levels and a dual safety lock, supporting 27 to 60 inch TVs at 88 lb.

The lock keeps the swivel from drifting when a child bumps the screen, which is the real safety value on a stand like this. It ranks sixth because it covers only up to 60 inch TVs, a smaller range than the Perlegear's 70 inches or the PERLESMITH's 75, though the swivel is just as wide as the Perlegear's. It lacks the Perlegear's tilt.

Buy it if you have a small to mid-size TV and children in the house. The caveat: the 60 inch limit rules out most newer living room sets.
products.idealFor: Families with a small to mid-size TV on a dresser.
products.skipIf: Your TV is larger than 60 inches.

products.name: Rfiver Universal Swivel Tabletop Stand
products.verdict: A 27 to 60 inch tabletop base with 6 height levels and an 8mm glass base.
products.description:
The Rfiver is a tabletop swivel base for 27 to 60 inch TVs, with a 30 degree swivel, 6 height levels spanning 18.5 to 24.4 inches, an 8mm glass base and 88 lb capacity. It has a 5-year warranty.

It ranks last because it has the fewest height levels, 6 against 9 on its rivals, and a 30 degree turn. It also lists the clearest height range, which is useful for matching the screen to a dresser. Against the HOLMAXD, it lacks the safety lock and the wide swivel.

Buy it if you have a small TV in a bedroom and a dresser to put it on. The caveat is that 18.5 to 24.4 inches of height is low for tall furniture.
products.idealFor: Bedroom setups with a small TV and a dresser.
products.skipIf: You want more height settings or a wide turn.

whatMatters.detail: Swivel is how far the TV can turn left and right. Many listings give a total, so 60 degrees can mean 30 each way. A wider turn lets one TV serve two seating areas. Check whether the figure is total or per side, and compare it with how far you actually need to turn.

The rating is the load the base and column can carry, and big TVs can approach it. Tabletop bases often stop at 88 to 99 lb, while the FITUEYES floor stand reaches 143 lb. Weigh your TV before buying, and avoid designs that list no rating.

A floor stand carries the TV on a column and needs no furniture. A tabletop base sits on a dresser or console you already own. The right choice depends on what you have, since a tabletop base puts the full weight on your furniture. Check the furniture's own load limit.

Height levels let you match the screen to your eye line. Nine levels give finer control than three. Look for the number of levels and, if listed, the range in inches, such as 18.5 to 24.4 inches on the Rfiver, then compare with your furniture height.

A safety lock stops the swivel from moving unexpectedly, which matters with children or pets. Some stands also use glass thick enough to resist cracking. Look for named locks, like the HOLMAXD's dual safety lock, and for an anti-tip feature on any tall column.

faq.q: Does a swivel stand work with any TV?
faq.a: Most support VESA mounting patterns and a size range. The FITUEYES handles up to 800x600mm and 85 inches, while the HOLMAXD stops at 60 inches. Check your TV's VESA pattern and weight against the listing.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with swivel stands?
faq.a: Trusting the swivel angle without reading whether it is total. A 60 degree total, like the Perlegear's, is 30 degrees each way. If you need to face a second room, choose a stand with a clearly wider turn.

faq.q: Is a floor stand worth it over a tabletop base?
faq.a: For TVs above 65 inches, yes. The FITUEYES carries 143 lb with no furniture, while tabletop bases like the Perlegear stop at 88 lb and depend on your dresser being strong enough.
Floor stands such as the WALI take one to two people and basic tools, while tabletop bases are quicker. Always attach the TV with the supplied screws and level it before adding the soundbar.

faq.q: How do I keep the swivel smooth?
faq.a: Keep the base clear of dust and avoid overloading it. Safety locks like the HOLMAXD's dual lock should be unlocked before turning the screen, and the joint should never be forced.

faq.q: Can a swivel stand tip over?
faq.a: Any tall stand with a TV can tip if bumped. Use the wall strap when provided, keep the base on a flat floor and prefer the FITUEYES for large sets because of its wide footprint.

finalTake: The FITUEYES Floor TV Stand with Swivel is the best swivel TV stand for most big-screen rooms because it carries 143 lb with no furniture. The WALI Floor Stand is the pick for rooms short on outlets. If you own a dresser, the Perlegear gives the widest tabletop turn and tilt, and the PERLESMITH adds a 10-year warranty for a low price.
